title: manifest.jsonl — headless-browser page capture
description: One page acquired through the headless-browser fallback (REQ-0035), for JS-rendered portals a plain GET cannot read. `status` is the load-bearing field: `downloaded` means the capture passed the shell-vs-content assertion, `shell_only` means the browser returned a well-formed HTML document containing none of the data. Those are NOT interchangeable, and HTTP 200 does not distinguish them — data.gov.in answers 200 with a 1 MB Nuxt shell carrying 1,850 characters of visible text, larger than a fully-rendered 407 KB page carrying 67,372. `text_chars` is measured after script/style removal, which is why it separates the two when byte size does not. Shell captures are written to a separate directory from real ones so a directory glob cannot mistake one for the other. An HTTP 4xx/5xx is `error` no matter how much text the error page carries — Playwright returns a response rather than raising, so a verbose error page would otherwise clear the text floor and record as `downloaded`. `dry_run` is a separate boolean, not a status: a mode must never overwrite a verdict, or a shell capture reads as a clean preview run.
